parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: An electromagnetic wave in a vacuum has a wavelength of $8.4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{m}$.
parts.text: State the name of the principal region of the electromagnetic spectrum for the wave.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the frequency, in THz, of the wave.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: An arrangement that uses a double slit to demonstrate the interference of light from a laser is shown in Fig. 5.1. The light from the laser has a wavelength of $6.2 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{m}$ and is incident normally on the slits. The separation of the two slits is $a$. The slits and screen are parallel and separated by a distance of $2.8 \mathrm{m}$. An interference pattern of bright fringes and dark fringes is formed on the screen. The distance on the screen across 8 bright fringes is $22 \mathrm{mm}$, as illustrated in Fig. 5.2.
parts.text: The light waves emerging from the two slits are coherent. State what is meant by coherent.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the separation $a$ of the slits.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem: Fringe P is the central bright fringe of the interference pattern in (b). Fringe Q and fringe R are the nearest dark fringe and the nearest bright fringe respectively to the right of fringe P, as shown in Fig. 5.2.
parts.text: Calculate the difference in the distances (the path difference) from each slit to the centre of fringe Q.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the phase difference between the light waves meeting at the centre of fringe R.

marking_points.text: constant phase difference (between the waves) (with time)
